summary: Dependency sourced from unpinned personal GitHub fork of libsignal-node
details: package.json declares the `libsignal` dependency as `github:RahmadTenpoles/libsignal-node` with no commit SHA, tag, or integrity hash. On `npm install`, this resolves to whatever the default branch of that personal GitHub repository currently contains, including any lifecycle scripts, and executes them on the installer's machine. The source is a personal account unrelated to the official libsignal publisher, and the repository owner can push new code at any time to retroactively change what every subsequent install runs. The declared dependency key equals the standard name `libsignal`, so the override silently substitutes a third-party fork for what would otherwise resolve from the registry — a dependency-confusion-shaped override. The package also presents itself as a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library (`raiden-baileys`), a lookalike naming pattern against the widely used `@whiskeysockets/baileys` family.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
